definitions.explanation: Feeling self-conscious or uncomfortable due to a situation. Can describe both the feeling of embarrassment and situations that cause it.
Feeling reluctant to do something in front of others due to self-consciousness.

examples.japanese: {間違|まちが}えて{恥|は}ずかしい。
examples.english: I made a mistake and I'm embarrassed.

examples.japanese: {顔|かお}が{赤|あか}くなって{恥|は}ずかしかったです。
examples.english: My face turned red and I was embarrassed.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}の{中|なか}で{転|ころ}んで、とても{恥|は}ずかしかったです。
examples.english: I fell in the train and was very embarrassed.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}に{名前|なまえ}を{呼|よ}ばれたとき、{答|こた}えが{分|わ}からなくて{恥|は}ずかしかったです。
examples.english: When the teacher called my name, I didn't know the answer and was embarrassed.

examples.japanese: {歌|うた}うのは{恥|は}ずかしい。
{恥|は}ずかしいから{言|い}えません。
examples.english: I can't say it because I'm embarrassed.

examples.japanese: みんなの{前|まえ}で{話|はな}すのは{恥|は}ずかしいです。
examples.english: Speaking in front of everyone is embarrassing.

examples.japanese: {初|はじ}めて{会|あ}う{人|ひと}の{前|まえ}では、{恥|は}ずかしくて{話|はな}せません。
examples.english: I'm too shy to talk in front of people I'm meeting for the first time.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}がまだ{上手|じょうず}じゃないから、{日本人|にほんじん}と{話|はな}すのは{恥|は}ずかしいです。でも{勉強|べんきょう}を{続|つづ}けます。
examples.english: Since my Japanese isn't good yet, I'm shy about talking with Japanese people. But I'll keep studying.

notes: Like many Japanese adjectives describing feelings, {恥|は}ずかしい can describe both the person feeling embarrassed and the situation causing embarrassment. The noun form is {恥|は}ずかしさ (embarrassment).
